title: claude-kit funnel config
description: Describes one repository to the task funnel: its base branch, its gate commands, which paths are source and which are tests, and which document each review lens reads. `kit config check` validates the same things this schema does, plus the ones a schema cannot see: whether the branch has a remote, whether the paths exist, and whether every name cross-references something real.

base.description: The branch every diff and every worktree starts from. Must exist as origin/<base>.

docs.description: Repo documents the funnel points at. Every value is a path relative to the repo root and has to exist.

entry.description: The always-loaded entry file, usually AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

pipeline.description: The document that owns the flow rules. It outranks the skill where they disagree.

prefix.description: One prefix per kind of change. The keys are what `worktree add --kind` accepts.

path.description: Where the worktree goes. Relative paths resolve against the main checkout, not the current directory. Placeholders: {repo} {issue} {slug}.

setup.description: Commands run inside a fresh worktree. If any fails the worktree is removed, so a half-installed environment never survives.

skipSetupWhenDocOnly.description: A doc-only scope skips setup, and then no gate command can run either: the gate becomes the commit alone.

gates.description: The commands that actually gate this repo. A gate is run by `kit gate` and gets a receipt keyed by the working tree's SHA, so the same command over the same tree is never paid twice.

cmd.description: Run through a shell from the repo root, so a compound command works. Placeholder: {base}.

stages.description: Which gates each funnel stage runs. Every name has to be a key of `gates`. The fix-round stage is where the incremental forms belong, because rounds are where the repetition is.

slices.description: Named git diff ranges. Each value is appended to `git diff`, so it carries both the range and the pathspec: `{base}...HEAD -- src ':(exclude)src/tests'`. A slice whose paths do not exist produces an empty diff, which downstream reads as nothing to review, so `kit config check` verifies the paths.

lenses.description: One entry per review lens. Lenses that share a slice are dispatched together as numbered parts of one contract, which is why the slice is the grouping key and not the lens.

docs.description: Only the documents this lens needs. The blanket set is the largest single cost in a review, paid once per dispatch at the most expensive tier.

grepTargets.description: Prose surfaces the claims lens checks for sentences the change falsified. `kit review` greps them for the declaration names and multi-digit literals the diff touched and hands over a candidate list, instead of the lens reading whole files.

effort.description: Which lenses each effort level runs. The level buys width in the first pass, not permission to iterate.

maxRounds.description: Cap on fix rounds. At the cap every open finding gets a written decision; silent discard is prohibited.

maxParallelAgents.description: Concurrency ceiling for read-only fan-out. Set it from the machine, not from the number of lenses: 3 to 5 is where published guidance lands, and a 6 GB box crashes above 4.

flaky.description: Known-flaky test files. A gate red in a file the diff never touched is a wasted fix round, so `kit gate` reports whether a failing file is on this list and whether this branch can even reach it. Each entry carries why, so the list can be emptied instead of growing.

board.description: Path to the board mapping, relative to the checkout that owns the config. Absent or missing means the funnel skips board moves instead of failing.
